source_text: Nemo conviciis felicem impudentiam, nemo maxillas palmis, nemo subiciet terga verberibus; nec conflare studebit de infirmitate virtutem; nec cum inopia frugalitas, nec cum moeroribus magnanimitas neminem iam ibi iustorum lividum facere corpus suum, et servituti subicere; neminem humiliare animam suam stratis duris et paedore membrorum Nec patientia cum dolore luctabitur
pass_a_gloss: No-one conviciis felicem impudentiam, no-one maxillas palmis, no-one subiciet terga verberibus; nor conflare studebit about/from infirmitate virtue; nor when/with lack frugalitas, nor when/with moeroribus magnanimitas neminem already there iustorum lividum to-make body his-own, and servituti subicere; neminem humiliare soul his-own stratis duris and paedore of-members nor patientia when/with dolore luctabitur.

lemmas.lexica: LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: None of the righteous there will any longer bruise his body and bring it into subjection. No one will humble his soul with a hard bed and bodily filth.

No one will expose his blessed disregard for shame to insults, his cheeks to slaps, or his back to lashes. Nor will he strive to forge strength out of weakness. Frugality will not struggle with poverty, nor greatness of soul with grief, nor patience with pain.

choices.why: Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
